annotations.description: Fetching a basic Plains with Flooded Strand when the hand contains Thundering Falls (which enters tapped anyway), two Solitudes (white-heavy), Arena of Glory, Sacred Foundry, and Quantum Riddler. The hand needs both white and blue mana going forward. Fetching Hallowed Fountain (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) would provide both a Plains and an Island, enabling future blue mana for Quantum Riddler while still providing white for the Solitudes. A basic Plains only provides white mana and doesn't advance the blue mana plan. Alternatively, Hallowed Fountain could enter tapped on turn 1 (since there's no 1-drop to cast) saving 2 life while still being a dual land for future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Plains with Flooded Strand.
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Hallowed Fountain, letting it enter tapped (no 1-mana play this turn anyway) to have access to both white and blue mana without paying life. This better supports casting Quantum Riddler later while still providing white for Solitude.

annotations.description: Evoking Solitude to remove Ragavan requires exiling the other Solitude from hand as the pitch cost, spending both copies of a premium card to remove a 1-mana creature. This is a massive resource expenditure (2-for-1 in premium cards) to answer a threat that, while dangerous, could potentially be dealt with more efficiently. The opponent also gains 2 life from Solitude's exile trigger.

annotations.description: Casting Phelia before combat means the opponent knows about it before declaring blockers, and more importantly, Phelia has flash so it could have been cast after combat or at end of opponent's turn. However, since there's no combat trick benefit to waiting (Phelia needs to attack to use her ability, so casting her main phase is fine for attacking next turn), the main concern is sequencing: playing a land first (Arena of Glory or Plains) before casting the spell would be better to preserve options. With Plains and Sacred Foundry untapped, they have exactly {1}{W} for Phelia, so no land drop is needed first. But they should consider whether holding up Solitude (which requires exiling a white card, not mana) might be better against Ragavan. On the other hand, Phelia on board provides a blocker against Ragavan and her flash means she could have been cast on opponent's end step instead, keeping mana open and maintaining ambiguity about what's in hand. Casting Phelia in main phase rather than at end of opponent's turn (using flash) gives away information unnecessarily.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd during precombat main phase on turn 2
annotations.betterLine: Since Phelia has flash, consider waiting to cast her at end of opponent's next turn's combat step or during their turn to block Ragavan, or simply play a land (like Plains or Arena of Glory) first to develop mana while keeping options open. Alternatively, holding priority to potentially evoke Solitude on Ragavan (exiling Phelia or Quantum Riddler as the white card pitch) could remove the Ragavan threat entirely, though that's card-intensive.

annotations.description: The player could evoke Solitude by exiling the other Solitude from hand to exile Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer. Ragavan is a dangerous threat that generates card advantage and treasures on combat damage. Evoke Solitude would remove Ragavan (opponent gains 2 life), and the player gains life from Solitude's lifelink body entering (though it gets sacrificed). This also triggers Guide of Souls if... wait, there's no Guide of Souls on the battlefield. Let me re-check. The battlefield has Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd, Plains (tapped), Sacred Foundry (tapped). So evoking Solitude exiles the other Solitude from hand, Solitude enters, its ETB exiles Ragavan (opponent gains 2 life), then Solitude is sacrificed. This is a 2-for-1 against yourself (spending two Solitudes to remove one Ragavan), but Ragavan left unchecked is very dangerous. However, the player has Phelia which can attack and exile Ragavan temporarily (flickering it). Actually, Phelia's trigger exiles 'up to one other target nonland permanent' when it attacks - so Phelia could exile Ragavan on attack. But the player skipped their attack phase too. The player declined to evoke Solitude AND skipped attacking with Phelia to exile Ragavan. Phelia attacking to exile Ragavan would be extremely strong - Ragavan gets exiled, returns at end step under opponent's control but without dealing combat damage this turn, and Phelia doesn't get the +1/+1 counter since it returns under the opponent's control. Actually wait - Phelia's trigger says 'if it entered under your control, put a +1/+1 counter on Phelia' - Ragavan returns under the opponent's control so no counter. But the key point is Phelia can attack into a 2/1 Ragavan. Ragavan could block and trade... no, Phelia is 2/2 vs Ragavan 2/1 so Phelia survives. But the opponent might not block. Either way, attacking with Phelia to exile Ragavan is very strong. The decision here was declining Solitude, but the player also skipped attacking with Phelia (noted in 'After'). The evoke Solitude line spending two cards to remove Ragavan is debatable, but not attacking with Phelia to temporarily exile Ragavan is a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast/evoke Solitude and then skipped combat entirely, leaving Ragavan unchecked.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd targeting Ragavan with Phelia's attack trigger to exile it for the turn, preventing Ragavan from attacking and generating value. Evoking Solitude (2-for-1ing yourself) is more debatable but the missed Phelia attack is clearly wrong.

annotations.description: Discarding Ocelot Pride to Seasoned Pyromancer is a significant mistake. Ocelot Pride is one of the best cards in the Boros Energy/tokens archetype - it creates tokens every end step when you gain life (easy with Guide of Souls on board), has first strike and lifelink, and can snowball with the city's blessing. Goblin Bombardment is a good card but Ocelot Pride is a key engine piece that synergizes perfectly with Guide of Souls already on the battlefield. Flooded Strand is a land that could be played for a land drop. The optimal discard would be Flooded Strand + Goblin Bombardment (both nonland cards discarded create elemental tokens, but keeping the most impactful card matters more). Actually, Seasoned Pyromancer creates tokens for each nonland card discarded - so discarding two nonland cards (Ocelot Pride + Goblin Bombardment) creates two 1/1 Elemental tokens, while discarding Flooded Strand + one nonland creates only one token. However, Ocelot Pride's long-term value far exceeds a 1/1 Elemental token. The player should have discarded Flooded Strand + Goblin Bombardment, keeping Ocelot Pride to deploy as a powerful threat that synergizes with Guide of Souls.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Ocelot Pride and Goblin Bombardment to Seasoned Pyromancer, losing a key engine creature for the sake of creating an extra 1/1 Elemental token.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Flooded Strand and Goblin Bombardment, keeping Ocelot Pride to play as a powerful synergy piece with Guide of Souls. Even getting one fewer Elemental token is worth preserving Ocelot Pride's snowball potential.

Phelia is a high-value creature with flash and flicker abilities, and Guide of Souls is an important engine piece for the opponent's energy/lifegain strategy.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Teferi, Time Raveler (1WU, easily payable with 8 lands) and immediately -3 to bounce Goblin Bombardment to opponent's hand, drawing a card and removing the instant-speed damage threat that could kill at 2 life.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing Goblin Bombardment (which converts any creature into direct damage), Gem25F Truth declined to cast Solitude during their combat step. Hard-casting Solitude (they have 8 lands, need 3WW which is available) would exile the Elemental Token (removing Bombardment ammunition), provide a 3/2 lifelink body that could attack to gain 3 life, significantly improving survival chances. At 2 life, every point of life and every creature the opponent has matters enormously with Goblin Bombardment on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting Solitude or cracking Scalding Tarn during combat
annotations.betterLine: Hard-cast Solitude targeting the Elemental Token to exile Bombardment fuel and gain a lifelink attacker to recover life total from the critical 2 life

annotations.description: At 2 life facing an opponent with Goblin Bombardment and an Elemental Token on board, passing the turn is almost certainly lethal. The opponent can sacrifice the Elemental Token to Goblin Bombardment to deal 1 damage, and any creature they draw or play can be sacrificed for the second point. Gem25F Truth had Solitude in hand which could exile the Elemental Token (removing a Bombardment sacrifice target) and gain life via lifelink, and Teferi, Time Raveler which could bounce Goblin Bombardment (the key threat enabling the sacrifice-for-damage kill). Playing Teferi to bounce Goblin Bombardment would remove the immediate lethal threat, and Solitude could be evoked to deal with creatures. Instead, they passed with 8 untapped lands and critical spells in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without casting any spells, leaving Solitude, Teferi Time Raveler, and Consign to Memory unused despite having plenty of mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Teferi, Time Raveler using -3 to bounce Goblin Bombardment and draw a card, removing the opponent's ability to sacrifice creatures for direct damage. This addresses the most immediate lethal threat at 2 life. Could also consider evoking Solitude to exile the Elemental Token.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life with no blockers. Qwen3 Spike has lethal on board: attack with the 1/1 Elemental Token (1 damage) then sacrifice it to Goblin Bombardment (1 damage) for exactly 2. Casting Blood Moon first is unnecessary and gives the opponent a window to respond (they have blue mana open for potential interaction like Consign to Memory or other counterspells) before their nonbasics become Mountains.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Blood Moon before attacking, despite having lethal on board.
annotations.betterLine: Go directly to combat, attack with Elemental Token for 1 damage, then sacrifice it to Goblin Bombardment targeting the opponent for the final 1 damage, winning the game immediately.

annotations.description: Blood Moon is on the stack and will turn all nonbasic lands into Mountains. Gem25F Truth has 8 lands, of which only 2 are basic Plains - the other 6 (Sacred Foundry, Arena of Glory, Meticulous Archive, Thundering Falls, Steam Vents, Hallowed Fountain) will all become Mountains. This means they will lose access to white and blue mana entirely, being unable to cast Teferi, Solitude, or Consign to Memory. Consign to Memory specifically counters... wait, it counters triggered abilities or colorless spells, not enchantment spells. However, they could have evoked Solitude (exile a white card from hand) in response - but that doesn't help with Blood Moon. Actually, the real issue is they should have cracked Flooded Strand from hand... wait, Flooded Strand is in hand. They can't play it because it's not their land drop timing during stack resolution. Actually, looking more carefully: the choices offered are 'Solitude' and 'Scalding Tarn' (Scalding Tarn is in graveyard, not hand - this might be a UI artifact). But Consign to Memory is in hand and costs {U} - it counters triggered abilities or colorless spells, NOT enchantment spells like Blood Moon, so it can't counter Blood Moon. The key question is whether they should respond to Blood Moon somehow. They could evoke Solitude to exile the Elemental Token (pitching a white card), but that doesn't stop Blood Moon. Under Blood Moon, they lose all white/blue sources except 2 Plains. Actually wait - they have 2 basic Plains, so they still have some white mana. They won't have blue mana though. The player declined to act, which means Blood Moon resolves. With 2 Plains they can still cast some white spells. This may actually be reasonable since they can't counter Blood Moon with anything in hand. Let me reconsider - the decline seems fine since Consign to Memory can't counter Blood Moon (it's not a triggered ability or colorless spell).
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to respond to Blood Moon on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Actually, on reflection, Consign to Memory cannot counter Blood Moon (it only hits triggered abilities or colorless spells), and no other response meaningfully stops it. However, they should have cracked Flooded Strand (if possible to play it first) before Blood Moon resolves to fetch a basic Island or Plains. Since Flooded Strand is in hand and can't be played during stack resolution, the decline may be forced. This is likely not a blunder.
